selected.title: Who takes the order
selected.texas_link: Wok & Karahi is a family-run restaurant in Spring, and Click2Houston datelines its report in Harris County. The film draws a generic small restaurant and names no person.

movement.action: reported that Wok & Karahi in Spring replaced its only server with an AI host that takes orders by table code and phone and requires payment before cooking
movement.object: AI host named Haniya with table QR ordering and pre-payment

selected.why_today: FOX 26 Houston reported the change on October 20th, 2026 after Muslim Mirror on October 19th, and KPRC Click2Houston followed on October 21st, 2026, as the restaurant reports kitchen staff now get all of the tips.
selected.consequence: The order now goes to software and is paid before the kitchen starts, and the restaurant says the kitchen staff now get 100 percent of tips.
selected.application_change: A server who greeted, took the order and ran the check is replaced by a host a guest reaches by table code or phone, with payment first and the kitchen ticket after.
selected.counter_image: Every dollar figure is the owner's own count, no outlet says whether the restaurant takes a tip credit, which decides whether a tip pool with cooks is allowed under federal rules, and one customer said QR codes don't suit people like her mother.
selected.earned_take: Software now takes the order, and who gets the tip rests on the owner's word.

agency.next_step: No agency action is reported. The Texas Workforce Commission guidance page describes the federal tip pool rule.
agency.who_can_act: The owner can show the pay and tip policy, and kitchen staff can ask the U.S. Department of Labor Wage and Hour Division or the Texas Workforce Commission about it.

filmability.viewer_question: When a restaurant loses its only server, who takes the order and who gets the tip?
filmability.opening_action: An illustrated guest scans a code on a restaurant table and a phone shows the menu, disclosed as Illustration.
filmability.mechanism: Input: a guest scans a table code or calls. Transformation: a host takes the order and the guest pays from a phone. Result: the kitchen ticket prints only after payment. Limit: the tip split and savings are the owner's own account.
filmability.human_consequence: The family could not keep the server job filled, the kitchen staff are said to get all of the tips, and a customer says QR codes don't suit her mother. No person is named.
filmability.source_limit: Every dollar figure is the owner's count. The tip claim has no pay record and no outlet says whether a tip credit is taken. The owner's name differs between outlets and the vendor is not identified. The restaurant's own web page does not mention the host.
three_key_images: An illustrated phone scanning a table code, with the menu opening on screen
A pay-first sequence where the kitchen ticket stays blank until the payment mark appears
A tip jar beside the kitchen pass with a label reading owner says all to the kitchen and a second tag reading no pay record shown
